text:
acme_prod: Our billing assistant started returning friendly confirmations but NOT invoking our billing tool after the optimizer rollout at ~2026-03-31T14:22Z. Expected a tool call but the model returned plain text. Small repro below. This started immediately after you flipped service-optimizer-v3 to 100% for our org.

acme_prod: Example (raw model output vs expected):
```
# user prompt
Charge invoice #12345 for $120

# expected (tool call JSON)
{"tool": "billing.charge", "args": {"invoice_id": "12345", "amount": 120}}

# actual model raw output
"Sure — I will charge invoice #12345 for $120."
```

acme_prod: Request ids: req_20260331_14_23_11, req_20260331_14_24_05. Model: gpt-redwood-00-finetune. Region: us-west-2. Rollout noted: service-optimizer-v3. We're on hosted API. This is blocking payment flows.

sam_support: Sorry — we’ll triage. Can you also paste a curl repro (header + body) and one raw response payload? Also are you seeing missing args (values present) or the whole tool call omitted?

acme_prod: Attaching quick curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-00-finetune","input":"Charge invoice #12345 for $120","metadata":{"client_request_id":"req_20260331_14_23_11"}}'
```
And raw response body: `{"id":"resp_abc","output":"Sure — I will charge invoice #12345 for $120."}` (no tool JSON emitted).

oliver_eng: tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml to triage, this reads like tool-call suppression rather than arg mangling. @maya_sre can you check deployment logs and if any request-mappers or tokenizer-level pruning was introduced in optimizer v3?

maya_sre: deploy-bot reported: "service-optimizer-v3 canary 2026-03-31T14:02Z -> 20% traffic; promoted to 100% 2026-03-31T14:22Z". No infra config changes at the same time, just the optimizer artifact.

julia_prod: From our side we saw a change in the prompt rewrite step inside optimizer v3: it adds a compacting pass that prunes low-signal token spans. Example diff of that pass (sanitized):
```
- "rewrite_passes": ["normalize_json", "preserve_tool_json"]
+ "rewrite_passes": ["normalize_json", "aggressive_prefix_prune"]
```
That new "aggressive_prefix_prune" looks like it can drop the tool JSON block if the model emits it as a short inline JSON in free text.

oliver_eng: OK that matches what we suspected. Possible mitigation: force the structured tool-json output by setting a generation override on the route: `force_tool_json=true` or pin the customer to pre-optimizer variant. I'll start a rollback canary for affected orgs.

sam_support: I've applied a temporary route override for acme_prod to use service-optimizer-v2 (previous variant) and forced `force_tool_json=true` for their requests. Can you validate on your side?

acme_prod: Confirmed — after routing change and adding the header X-Redwood-Force-Tool-Json: 1 our test requests now include the JSON tool invocation again (checked req_20260331_14_40_02). Payment flow resumed. Thanks. :thumbsup:

oliver_eng: We'll open a postmortem and add an e2e test asserting JSON tool calls survive optimizer rewrites. Short-term: we will revert the aggressive prune in v3 and release v3.1 with explicit preservation of tool tokens. Long-term: add a configurable guardrail on optimizer that refuses to remove bracketed/json-like spans when tool_calling is enabled. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml for fix and a follow-up with customer success.

sam_support: Apologies again to ACME team — we'll keep this thread updated with rollback PRs and ETA for v3.1.

acme_prod: Appreciate the fast response. Please keep us posted, we can provide more logs if needed.
